destination.name: Wollongong
destination.tagline: A coastal city of surf beaches beneath the Illawarra escarpment.
destination.description: Wollongong is a coastal city south of Sydney, never more than about 6 km wide but stretching over 40 km from south to north between the escarpment and the sea. It has 17 surf beaches with free foreshore parking. The Grand Pacific Drive passes over Sea Cliff Bridge, a 665 m road bridge, and escarpment lookouts such as Sublime Point and Mount Keira look over the city and coast. At Berkeley, Nan Tien Temple is the largest Buddhist temple in Australia.

goodToKnow.title: Easy by train
goodToKnow.detail: NSW TrainLink runs from Sydney every 15–30 minutes on weekdays and every 60 minutes on weekends; Wollongong Station is in the CBD.

goodToKnow.title: Temple hours
goodToKnow.detail: Nan Tien Temple is free and open 9 am–5 pm; Wikivoyage lists Tue–Sun, with Mondays only on public holidays, so check before going.

goodToKnow.title: Beach patrols
goodToKnow.detail: Austinmer Beach is patrolled September to April, while North Wollongong Beach is patrolled all year.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} are the summer months for the city's 17 surf beaches.
